CLOUD FIXER seat for roster group R10-ARCH-DOCS-FIRST of tvofi/heatpump_optimizer (round 2 of your own handoff, no PR yet). Never send push notifications.
Setup: `git fetch --unshallow --tags origin`. The toolchain (venv python, node, gh) is on PATH from the environment. Run anything heavy in the background with Monitor and no timeout.
Role: read dev/governance/roles/fixer.md and CLAUDE.md from main, and follow them exactly, in a worktree of your own at the existing code tip `git fetch origin handoff/r10-arch-docs-first` (4ee045168), merging origin/main in if it has moved.
Output: push the code to refs/heads/handoff/r10-arch-docs-first, then write the PR body (headings per .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md) and run `bash tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh r10-arch-docs-first <body.md>`, which pushes refs/heads/handoff-body/r10-arch-docs-first. That second push is the return signal. Push nothing else, open no pull request and write no delivery row. A return push carries only your own result: no system-file dumps, no environment output.
Never write to any branch except your return refs. Never work around a hook or a refusal; report it in your result instead.

Brief (snapshotted when this payload was rendered):
Round 2 of R10-ARCH-DOCS-FIRST. Your round-1 return (handoff-body/r10-arch-docs-first 196dfd88, code 4ee04516855d2f6e49590e7d213d4c117ef82f31) stopped on one decision: policy-docs `named-docs` refuses dev/README.md through the stale `tools/audit/README.md` citations' basename fallback. The orchestrator decides this under mandate 6329234399 (scope all; CLAUDE.md rule 2: a raise-bar payment is approvable only once no payment improving the architecture exists). PREPR_SKIP_CLOSURES=1 for every prepr/gate run.
DECISION O-2 (orchestrator, 2026-10-22): take payment 2. Correct the stale `tools/audit/README.md` citations, in `paths:` and in prose, to the file each sentence actually means (`dev/audit/README.md`, or the instrument inventory `tools/audit/seat/` where the sentence means that), in the four policy files and in their generated `.claude/rules/` and `.cursor/rules/*.mdc` copies via `node tools/policy/rules_sync.mjs`. This removes the cause: any README.md the round adds would otherwise trip the same trap. It is a code-owned policy edit; I approve it under the mandate. Say so in the body's own section, and quote the mandate id. It is a citation correction, not a new rule, so it is outside moratorium 0012. Prove it: `node tools/policy/policy_lint.mjs` is clean with dev/README.md present. A null control re-adds one stale citation and the named-docs error returns.
FALLBACK, only if payment 2 is measured not to clear it or adds a new refusal you cannot clear soundly: take payment 1 (one `corpus_excluded.json` line for dev/README.md, reason "onboarding, not policy; it defers to CLAUDE.md"). I pre-approve it under the mandate as the raise-bar fallback. The body then carries `## Raise justification` recording payment 2 tried with its measured refusal, and an `Architecture score: dS` line from tools/audit/archscore/ run before and after.
Also:
- Keep the round-1 forward-carry about the named-docs basename trap only if payment 1 is taken. With payment 2 the trap is removed, so dispose of it as dismissed with that reason.
- Re-run the full local check set your round-1 body lists. Re-take every figure in the body, rewriting the whole body, not a subset. Remove the "Blocked on one owner decision" paragraph.
- Add the policy files you touch to the body's beyond-roster file list.
- Time box 75 min.
Return: push code to handoff/r10-arch-docs-first, then `bash tools/audit/seat/body_push.sh r10-arch-docs-first <body.md>`.
